key_insight: OCSF separates clinical-note encoding from ontology indexing, allowing one trained model to switch medical code sets without target-specific training.
clinical_relevance: The approach could reduce retraining burdens when coding standards change, though real-world coding accuracy and workflow value remain to be established.
method: Encode each note into a fixed-size 2D clinical state matrix without code-specific parameters.
Compile ontology descriptions offline into a Tikhonov deconvolution operator to reduce interference between sibling codes.
Apply the compiled operator to read out codes without target-specific tuning.
evidence_signal: Trained only on English MIMIC-IV ICD-9 discharge summaries, OCSF was evaluated across 58,706 held-out notes and five unseen ontologies, reporting 63.15% in-domain Micro-F1 and 29.23% recall at gold cardinality for English ICD-10.
watch_item: Recall measured using the true number of codes per note does not establish performance when that number is unknown in routine coding.
paper_title: Ontology-Compiled 2D Clinical State Fields with Bidirectional Diffusion Encoders for Zero-Training Cross-Ontology Medical Coding
